facts: The paper is titled "Understanding and Improving Information Preservation in Prompt Compression for LLMs."
Weronika Łajewska is affiliated with the University of Stavanger.
The research addresses challenges related to information loss in prompt compression techniques.
The authors propose methods to improve the retention of essential content in compressed prompts.
Recent advancements in large language models have led to their application in various tasks.
Prompt compression techniques have been developed to balance input length and performance.
Improvements of up to 23% in downstream performance were achieved through refined soft prompting.
The optimal trade-off was found with soft prompting combined with sequence-level training.
Recent advancements in large language models have enabled their application to tasks requiring long-context input.
Research has focused on prompt compression methods to reduce input length while preserving essential information.
The framework is applied to analyze hard-prompting method LLMLingua and soft-prompting methods xRAG and PISCO.
PISCO achieves the best balance between compression and effectiveness.
Prompt compression enhances the efficiency of large language models (LLMs) by creating smaller, approximate representations of prompts.
Hard prompting focuses on producing concise text versions while retaining key information.
Notable soft prompting approaches include AutoCompressors, Gisting, ICAE, 500xCompressor, and xRAG.
Evaluation of these methods typically involves downstream tasks such as classification and QA.
The framework proposes including generation tasks with longer contexts for evaluating prompt compression methods.
Key evaluation dimensions include downstream task performance, response grounding, and information preservation.
Metrics like BERTScore and Exact Match are utilized for performance evaluation.
Performance data from models like Mistral-7B shows relative drops in performance when context is altered or removed.

The analysis evaluates four prompt compression methods using the Mistral-7B Instruct v0.2 model. PISCO employs two adapters for context compression and response generation. Performance assessments reveal significant performance drops (3% to 55%) with compression, particularly in complex tasks like HotpotQA. PISCO maintains higher semantic similarity and entity retention compared to xRAG.
The xRAG model has limitations in preserving detailed information during long-context scenarios.
The authors propose a modification called xRAG w/ Sentence PT + FT to enhance single-sentence sample handling.
The two-step pre-training method, xRAG w/ Two-Step PT + FT, achieves a 23% relative improvement in certain datasets.
PISCO is noted for achieving superior compression rates without performance loss in long-context scenarios.
Many methods, such as xRAG, struggle to preserve detailed information.
Modifications to xRAG show promise in improving information retention.
PISCO utilizes multi-token context understanding for better grounding.
A hybrid approach combining hard and soft prompting is proposed to minimize information loss.
The paper evaluates the quality of prompt compression methods in long-context generation tasks.
The study identifies that some existing methods struggle to maintain detailed information in long-context scenarios.
The proposed improvements to the xRAG soft compression method resulted in a 23% increase in downstream tasks.
The code repository for this research is available at https://github.com/amazon-science/information-preservation-in-prompt-compression.
The study exclusively uses Mistral-7B as the target large language model.
The analysis is confined to English benchmarks.
The evaluation includes only one representative baseline from each category of prompt compression techniques.
Further exploration is warranted in long-form question-answering scenarios.
The xRAG model was trained using the Mistral-7B Instruct v0.2 LLM.
Training was conducted on two compute instances with 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs over approximately 16 hours.
The training datasets comprised over 26 million Wikipedia snippets.
Mistral-7B achieved the highest grounding scores in a comparative analysis of grounding scores and information preservation.
